import io

    csv_data = """survived,pclass,sex,age,sibsp,parch,fare,embarked,class,who,adult_male,deck,embark_town,alive,alone
0,3,male,22.0,1,0,7.25,S,Third,man,True,,Southampton,no,False
1,1,female,38.0,1,0,71.2833,C,First,woman,False,C,Cherbourg,yes,False
1,3,female,26.0,0,0,7.925,S,Third,woman,False,,Southampton,yes,True
1,1,female,35.0,1,0,53.1,S,First,woman,False,C,Southampton,yes,False

"""
    df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and a set of subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(16, 12))
fig.suptitle('Comprehensive Analysis of Titanic Survival Factors', fontsize=20, weight='bold')

# --- Plot 1: Survival Rate by Passenger Class and Sex ---
sns.barplot(ax=axes[0, 0], data=df, x='class', y='survived', hue='sex', palette='viridis', errorbar=None)

axes[0, 0].bar_label(axes[0, 0].containers[0], fmt='%.2f')

axes[0, 0].legend(title='Sex')


# --- Plot 2: Age Distribution of Survivors vs. Non-Survivors ---
sns.kdeplot(ax=axes[0, 1], data=df, x='age', hue='survived', fill=True, common_norm=False, palette='crest')
axes[0, 1].set_title('Age Distribution by Survival Status', fontsize=14, weight='bold')
axes[0, 1].set_xlabel('Age')
axes[0, 1].set_ylabel('Density')
axes[0, 1].legend(title='Survived', labels=['Yes', 'No'])

# --- Plot 3: Survival Rate by Port of Embarkation ---
sns.countplot(ax=axes[1, 0], data=df, x='embark_town', hue='survived', palette='magma')
axes[1, 0].set_title('Survival Count by Port of Embarkation', fontsize=14, weight='bold')
axes[1, 0].set_xlabel('Port of Embarkation')
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel('Passenger Count')
axes[1, 0].legend(title='Survived', labels=['No', 'Yes'])

# --- Plot 4: Fare Distribution by Class and Survival ---
sns.stripplot(ax=axes[1, 1], data=df, x='class', y='fare', hue='survived', palette='rocket', dodge=True, alpha=0.5, jitter=0.3)
axes[1, 1].set_title('Fare Distribution by Class and Survival', fontsize=14, weight='bold')
axes[1, 1].set_xlabel('Passenger Class')
axes[1, 1].set_ylabel('Fare')
axes[1, 1].set_ylim(-5, 300) # Limit y-axis to see the distribution better, excluding extreme outliers
axes[1, 1].legend(title='Survived', labels=['No', 'Yes'])


# Adjust layout to prevent labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.95])

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
